subject.title: Allow before_agent_start hooks to override prompt

question: May an installed plugin with prompt-injection permission silently replace the current user prompt, and if so what precedence and audit/transcript semantics must every runner enforce?
rationale: The existing API intentionally permits additive prompt mutation, but full replacement grants materially greater authority over user intent and affects security, observability, transcript truth, and cross-harness compatibility.

options.title: Add guarded replacement
options.body: Extend `before_prompt_build`, inherit it in the legacy hook, reuse the established prompt-injection policy, and require deterministic precedence plus audit and cross-harness tests.

options.title: Require a separate privilege
options.body: Add replacement only behind a distinct plugin capability if maintainers judge additive injection and full intent rewriting to be different trust levels.

options.title: Keep hooks additive
options.body: Reject replacement and document `before_agent_run` blocking or a context-engine implementation as the supported response to oversized current prompts.

recommendation.title: Add guarded replacement
recommendation.body: Extend `before_prompt_build`, inherit it in the legacy hook, reuse the established prompt-injection policy, and require deterministic precedence plus audit and cross-harness tests.
